links.outcome: False-positive CADe detection boxes per case in general EGD
links.effect: Average 6.2 false-positive detections per case; PPV 0.62% under WLI and 2.45% under LCI. Biopsy rates (22.9% vs 16.2%) and exam time were not significantly increased.
links.quote: CADe exhibited an average of 6.2 false-positive detections per case.

unlisted_practices: Using CADe with image-enhanced endoscopy (linked-color imaging) rather than white-light imaging to reduce false-positive detections (3.48 vs 7.70 per case, P < .001)

openai.sample_unit: patients in propensity-score-matched comparison (105 CADe and 105 controls)

links.outcome: False-positive detections under different endoscopic imaging modes
links.effect: Mean false-positive boxes were 7.70 (4.81) with WLI versus 3.48 (2.55) with LCI; P < .001.
links.quote: Overall, the average number of false-positive detection boxes was 7.70 (4.81) and 3.48 (2.55) for WLI and LCI, respectively.

links.outcome: False-positive detections by H pylori infection status
links.effect: WLI false positives: 5.1 (3.7), 10.6 (5.2), and 8.9 (4.6) for uninfected, current, and past infection; LCI: 1.9 (1.7), 5.6 (2.9), and 3.8 (2.3), respectively.
links.quote: In the state of H pylori infection, both LCI and WLI showed significantly higher false-positive rates for current and past infection cases than for uninfected cases.

links.outcome: Gastric cancer detection by endoscopists with versus without CADe
links.effect: Detection was 4.8% with CADe versus 0.95% in matched controls; absolute difference 3.85% (95% CI, 0.67%-8.29%; P = .098), reported as not statistically significant.
links.quote: After matching, 1 GC was detected among 105 patients in the control group (0.95%), with an absolute difference of 3.85% (95% CI, 0.67%-8.29%; P = .098).

unlisted_practices: Use linked-color imaging rather than white-light imaging during gastric CADe to reduce false-positive detections.

links.effect: The GC detection rate was 4.8% in the CADe group versus 1.8% in the control group (difference of 3.0%), which was not statistically significant (p=0.07).
links.quote: The GC detection rate in the CADe group was slightly higher than in the control group (difference, 3.0%; 95% CI, 0.3%-6.3%), although the difference was not statistically significant ( P = .07).
